messages.text: Shop···· Is an order I placed in July 2026. I received the NerdOctaxe in September, and set it up to mine shortly thereafter, and it has been running since then. I checked on it today, and it was powered off completely. The power supply does not light up, and when I meter the cable that would plug into the miner, it reads 0 volts. It appears the power supply has failed.
I'm H., HeliumDeploy's technical specialist. Let me check our triage notes on this.

I'm H., HeliumDeploy's technical specialist. Sarah passed your message over to me.

What you are describing reads like a dead power supply rather than a dead miner: no LED on the brick and 0 V at the plug means nothing is reaching the Octaxe at all. On the NerdOctaxe family, a brick that quits after a couple of months of continuous running is by far the most common cause of "it was just off one morning".

One check before I call it, because it is the one thing that fakes the same symptom:

1. Plug the power supply into a different wall outlet, ideally on another circuit, and not through a power strip, surge bar or timer.
2. If that outlet is on a GFCI or an RCD, press reset on it first.
3. Tell me whether the LED on the brick comes on, and if you can, re-meter the output plug there.

If it is still dark and still 0 V on a known-good outlet, the brick is gone and the miner itself is almost certainly fine. If you happen to have another supply of the same rating handy, trying it would settle it outright, but do not force anything with a lower rating since the Octaxe pulls more than a generic phone brick can give.
I plugged the power supply into a different circuit. No LED on the brick, and 0 volts when I read the connector.

That settles it: the power supply is dead, not the miner.

No LED and 0 V at the output on two separate circuits means the brick is not regulating at all. There is nothing to fix inside it and nothing you should open, so the fix is a replacement supply. A failed brick after a couple of months of 24/7 duty is the single most common failure we see on the NerdOctaxe and Bitaxe family, and the board almost always survives it untouched.

Two things worth knowing in the meantime:

1. Do not substitute a weak brick to test it. The O. wants a supply that can hold its rated voltage at several amps. A phone charger or an underrated adapter can brown out and stress the voltage regulator on the board, which is the one failure that would turn this into a real problem.
2. If you own a correctly rated supply with the same connector and polarity, it is safe to try, and if the unit boots and hashes, that confirms the diagnosis completely.

I have written my findings up and passed them to the team with the part you need noted. They pick this up Monday at 10am ET and the answer comes to your email, so you do not need to sit in the chat.

If you want a faster read in the meantime, our Discord is very active: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , mention @nullhashrate (JD, our hardware lead). He knows these bricks well and can confirm the exact spec to look for.
